interactions.summary: After hearing one more imperfect-versus-perfect formulation, Jiang finally gives his own stripped-down model: absolute will is the soul's relation to God, while contingent will is the body's fearful response inside the material world.
A student asks whether the two wills can coexist, and Jiang answers by multiplying the model: the will exists across infinite dimensions that a person must try to harmonize.
Students translate harmony into balance or even godhood, but Jiang rejects self-deification and says the point is not to become God but to become closer to God.

claims.claim: Jiang's simplified model says absolute will is the soul always connected to God, while contingent will is the body's worldly and fearful mode of response.
Jiang says Piccarda's problem is that her absolute will stayed loyal to God while her contingent will surrendered in fear, creating a split inside the self.
Jiang expands Dante's two-will picture into a broader anthropology in which the will exists across infinite dimensions, and human work is to create harmony by aligning those layers.
Jiang rejects the idea that harmonizing wills makes a person into God; the aim is likeness or closeness to God, not self-deification.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang blows open Dante's tidy pair into an interior cosmos by saying the will exists in infinite dimensions that must somehow be brought into harmony.
signature_moments.source_phrase: you can think of the will existing in infinite dimensions
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is the packet's boldest conceptual leap and the clearest compression of Jiang's psychology of divided agency.

signature_moments.moment: The whole distinction snaps into one stark bodily contrast: soul stays with God while the body gets afraid.
signature_moments.source_phrase: the soul is always in connection with the God. Contingent will is the body
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is Jiang's first clean formulation that makes the Piccarda problem intelligible in ordinary language.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's expansion of Dante's dual-will language into a many-layered model of inner alignment rather than a strict binary only.
The state Jiang says a person seeks by aligning absolute and contingent expressions of will across different layers of the self.

chronology_notes.note: This June 15 packet is the first clean Jiang formulation of the absolute-versus-contingent-will problem, moving from soul-versus-body to a multi-dimensional harmony model whose goal is closeness to God rather than godhood.
